chunks: And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no Salat for the two Eids except with an Imam. So if you pray alone, there is no harm in it.

key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray Eid prayers alone if an Imam is not available?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies the juristic status of Eid prayers by distinguishing between the ideal congregational form (Jama'ah) and the validity of individual performance. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that while the Imam's presence is the normative condition for the ritual's completeness, the prayer remains valid even if offered alone, ensuring no religious detriment to the individual. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding communal obligations when circumstances prevent full congregation.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2. And from the previous chain from al-Hussain b. Sa’eed from Uthman b. Isa from Sama’a b. Mihran from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:
“Salaat of Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid- e-Qurbaan can be offered only in congregation. However if one wishes to offer it alone there is no harm in it.”
